notice: A teaching and evidence-tracing dataset, not a laboratory protocol or prediction engine.

evidenceLevels.label: Demonstrated
evidenceLevels.meaning: Documented result in the named domain and species. Does not generalize automatically to humans.

evidenceLevels.label: Documented proposal
evidenceLevels.meaning: A directly observable written proposal or correspondence, not proof that its aims succeeded.

evidenceLevels.label: Ethics guidance
evidenceLevels.meaning: Professional guidance or policy, not experimental evidence.

evidenceLevels.label: Unverified outcome
evidenceLevels.meaning: No confirming result is included in the cited source set.

claims.title: Dolly was cloned from an adult mammalian cell
claims.short: Dolly was born in 1996; the Roslin Institute documents her as the first mammal cloned from an adult cell.
claims.interpretation: The result belongs to animal reproductive biology, not human clinical feasibility.
limitations: Not evidence of any cloned human.
Does not define clinical success rates for other species.

claims.title: Animal nuclear transfer and human reproductive cloning are distinct claims
claims.short: Animal nuclear-transfer demonstrations show specific animal outcomes and do not themselves establish human reproductive cloning.
claims.interpretation: Do not assume techniques generalize across species or contexts.
limitations: No human cloning result is claimed.

claims.title: Cellular reprogramming to pluripotency is established science
claims.short: The 2012 Nobel Prize recognized work demonstrating that mature cells can be reprogrammed to pluripotency.
claims.interpretation: Producing pluripotent cells is not producing a cloned organism.
limitations: Cell cultures are not human births.

claims.title: Genetic engineering and cloning are not equivalent
claims.short: Cloning and intentional genome editing answer different questions about inheritance and biological variation.
claims.interpretation: A gene-edited animal need not be a clone, and a clone need not be gene-edited.
limitations: Descriptions here are conceptual, not procedural.

claims.title: Bishop publicly advanced human embryo genetic-engineering proposals
claims.short: Bryan Bishop's public FAQ outlines proposed avenues for human embryo genetic engineering.
claims.interpretation: This verifies that ideas were proposed publicly. It does not establish successful reproductive experiments.
limitations: Self-authored proposal rather than independent confirmation.

claims.title: An August 2018 email described a proposed cloning-related company
claims.short: Released correspondence describes a proposed designer-baby and human-cloning company and a five-year funding request.
claims.interpretation: Documented intent and budget are not proof of financing, laboratory implementation, or a human-cloning result.
limitations: Archive transcription should be checked against original release.
No actual investment established by this email.

claims.title: Bishop's project produced a cloned human
claims.short: The reviewed source set does not contain independent scientific verification of a cloned human produced by Bishop's project.
claims.interpretation: Treat success claims as unsupported pending credible independent publication and verification.
limitations: Absence from this curated dataset cannot establish every event that occurred.
No human cloning method or outcome is represented.

claims.title: Human reproductive cloning is identified as a prohibited activity in ISSCR guidance
claims.short: The ISSCR's guidelines distinguish human reproductive cloning from permitted laboratory stem-cell research.
claims.interpretation: Professional ethical guidance is a normative research boundary rather than evidence of an experiment.
limitations: Consult current local law and institutional rules for specific questions.

claims.title: A clone would not copy the source individual's memories or identity
claims.short: Genetic similarity does not encode the memories, learned skills, developmental history or personality of an existing individual.
claims.interpretation: Nuclear DNA is only one component of a person's development and identity.
limitations: Memory and personhood are not measured by this application.
